Any caller holding a raw pointer into dat->chain across this call is left with a dangling pointer. The wrapper itself is clean, but it is a realloc trigger.

If the caller passed a pointer that aliases dat->chain (e.g. a string stored in the same buffer), the realloc at line 3015 triggered by the writes invalidates 'chain', and line 2150 then reads freed memory. Same pattern in bit_write_TU16 (line 2166) and bit_write_T32 (line 2182).

Reported as low-confidence because the stale pointer is not dereferenced after the write.

The free is after the last use, so this is not a UAF — but the loop at 1853 calls bit_write_RC which may realloc dat->chain; if bit_embed_TU ever returned a pointer into dat->chain (it does not today, it mallocs), this would be a UAF. Flagged only as a low-confidence structural note.
